R7.6.response:
Both observations are correct, and checking the second one carefully showed it was worse than described.

On the missing curves: the submitted Section VII-E discussed ROC behavior for the baselines without presenting a single curve. The revision adds them for every method, measured by us on the full chronological test partition, and pairs each ROC curve with a precision-recall curve on the same axes. The pairing is the substance rather than a convention. At 97.17 percent positive prevalence a classifier predicting at random attains average precision equal to that prevalence, so the majority baseline sits at AP 0.9717 with ROC-AUC 0.5000, and the gap between a model's two numbers measures how much the imbalance flatters its ROC curve. The decision tree makes the point sharply: ROC-AUC 0.6075 reads as though the model were doing something, while its average precision of 0.9777 is six thousandths above chance. Logistic regression is within 0.0014 of chance. Only the precision-recall panel reveals this. Our detector reaches ROC-AUC 0.999728 with a bootstrap interval of [0.99970, 0.99975] and average precision 0.999992.

On the caption mismatch: the caption of the figure in question stated "Left: ROC curve and FPR vs. threshold", but the panel contains no ROC curve. It plots accuracy against threshold on one axis and false positive rate on the other. The caption further claimed zero false negatives below a threshold of 0.5 and zero false positives at 0.9, neither of which the figure shows, and stated that accuracy remains at 100 percent across window sizes when the axis is labelled 99.998 percent plus an offset. The threshold symbol also rendered as the literal string "au" in both axis labels, because the mathematics delimiters had been lost in the figure source, which is the same defect Reviewer 1 identified in the Figure 2 graphic.

We have not repaired that figure. The sweep it reported was measured under the stratified random split that Section VII-A corrects, so it is not comparable with anything else in the revision, and we do not carry it over. The hyperparameter section now states which of the two hyperparameters was selected, where it was selected, and that the entropy window length was fixed before any evaluation and never tuned, together with the reason a sweep on this corpus would be fitted to noise. We would rather report the absence of a sweep than reprint one produced under a protocol we have withdrawn.
R7.6.action: Added ROC and precision-recall curves for every method on the full chronological partition, with bootstrap intervals and the chance average-precision baseline marked. Removed the mislabelled sensitivity figure rather than recaptioning it, and rewrote the hyperparameter section to state what was selected, where, and what was not tuned.
